comparison: v0.6.2 versus v0.7.0; both modules built in release profile with the same toolchain against one native nginx 1.31.10 (./configure --with-compat); the v0.7.0 load generator drives both

host.note: desktop host with other workloads; one-minute load average between 3 and 8 during the HTTP runs

engine_cpu.command: POW_BENCH_CPU=1 cargo bench --locked -p pow-gate-core --features native-crypto --bench engine -- --sample-size 20 --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 1
engine_cpu.note: three alternating runs per tree; thread CPU time; values are Criterion point estimates in nanoseconds. Criterion 0.5 (before) and 0.8 (after).

request_path_tuning.comparison: v0.7.0 before the request-path tuning (commit c6b299b, the "after" build above) versus the tuned tree; same nginx, toolchain and load generator

profile.method: perf record -e cpu-clock:u -F 4999, one nginx process (master_process off) pinned to CPU 0, cleared mode, 16 clients; user-space samples only

engine_cpu.note: three runs of the tuned tree; v0.7.0 values are the after_median_ns figures in engine_cpu above

state_file.comparison: the tuned module without (before) and with (after) pow_gate_state_file pointing at an existing file, so the restored path with its pre-restart floor is active; one pinned worker; nginx is given 1.2 s after start so challenges are not issued in the restart second

startup.method: nginx -t -q, 200 runs per configuration, three passes, median/minimum wall-clock ms; state file on tmpfs, so the one fsync at creation costs nothing here
